terra.problem: The joke equates a mountain below the hills with a dip in a road. The comparison doesn't make sense.
The passage says all nations will stream to the mountain and many peoples will say to come. It doesn't say an invitation is going out widely.
Saying the peoples aren't climbing for a view rules out a motive the text doesn't address.
The text doesn't establish that nobody on the mountain is asking about crowns.
The classroom trip comparison brings a school scenario into the joke.
After the quotation, the explanation repeats the same fact twice without a distinct Papa Dorin voice.
The trade-in joke changes the action: the swords are beaten into plowshares, not exchanged in a deal.
No more swords raised is broader than the text, which says nation will no longer take up the sword against nation.
The invitation is to walk in the light of the LORD, not explicitly to go up the mountain. Also, let us doesn't establish that the prophet is already walking with them.
The explanation is a generic correction that quotes and repeats the answer without a distinct Papa Dorin voice.
I'll be gentle about it comments on how Papa Dorin is telling the passage.
The explanation simply rejects the option, quotes the verse, and repeats the answer. It sounds generic rather than like Papa Dorin.
